emcap-alchemy-2:ashbyhq:bf5d849a-d0da-41.description: About Alchemy Alchemy is the Web3 infrastructure and developer platform that powers millions of users and the world’s most innovative blockchain applications. From enabling $1+ trillion in financial transactions worldwide to scaling L2s and enabling DeFi, Alchemy provides the infrastructure and tools developers need to build reliable, scalable, and accessible experiences. Trusted by companies like JPMorgan, Stripe, Visa, Franklin Templeton, Nike, and backed by a16z, Coatue, Silver Lake, Lightspeed, and Stanford University, Alchemy is building the foundational layer for a decentralized and AI-enabled Web3 ecosystem. For more information, visit alchemy.com http://alchemy.com. About the Role Alchemy is hiring a Social & Technical Content Manager to own how our strongest product, engineering, and customer stories show up online. This is a social-first role focused initially on X and LinkedIn, with opportunities to extend strong ideas into video, email, events, and longer-form content. You have strong social instincts, a sharp editorial eye, and enough technical curiosity to earn the trust of engineers. You can find the idea worth building around, choose the right format, and carry an incomplete brief through to a finished package. You prefer a few stories with a clear point of view to filling a calendar for its own sake. What You’ll Do - Own day-to-day editorial planning and execution for Alchemy's social channels, with a primary focus on X. - Help shape channel strategy with Marketing leadership: identify our core content pillars, build the brand of internal Alchemists, and experiment with ambassadors, KOLs, and other growth levers. - Build a reliable story pipeline with Product Marketing, Product, Engineering, Developer Relations, Customer Success, and the broader Marketing team. - Interview engineers, product leaders, customers, and executives to find the detail that makes a story credible. - Turn launch briefs, product demos, technical documentation, engineering interviews, and customer results into platform-native social posts, videos, emails, and longer-form content. - Develop repeatable content pillars, formats, and distribution plans that extend important launches and customer stories beyond launch day. - Partner with designers and video producers while owning the idea, message, script, and editorial bar. - Help Alchemy's experts show up on social with posts that sound like them. - Use AI to move faster on research, drafting, repurposing, and analysis. Use performance data to decide what to repeat or stop. What we’re looking for - 3+ years creating social or technical content for a company, product, or expert. - Work samples that show strong storytelling, including at least one social-first example and one piece that makes a technical subject clear. - Strong instincts for social media. You understand how each platform works and know when a format or trend serves the story. - Clear, concise writing and rigorous editing. You can simplify a complex idea without making it less accurate. - Technical curiosity and the confidence to learn from documentation, demos, and subject-matter experts. You do not need to be an engineer, but you should know when a claim needs verification before publishing. - Sound editorial judgment. You can choose what deserves amplification, cut what does not, and finish the work with limited oversight. - Experience earning trust across technical and creative teams, managing feedback, and keeping launches moving. - A practical approach to measurement. You can explain what worked, what did not, and what you would change. - The ability to develop strong video concepts and scripts. On-camera work and video editing are useful, but not required. - You might come from social media, developer relations, technical content, developer education, or product marketing. Experience in developer tools, infrastructure, AI, fintech, cybersecurity, or Web3 is helpful. Prior Web3 experience is not required. Benefits and Pe

jobgether-jobgether:lever:4b311679-cff5-.description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior Software Engineer (Go) based in Australia. This is an opportunity to join a Platform Engineering team focused on improving the developer experience across a global technology environment. You will design and build high-performance backend services, APIs, microservices, and CLI tools using Go. The role has a strong focus on automation, self-service infrastructure, governance-as-code, and scalable internal platforms. You’ll work with Kubernetes, AWS, GitHub, databases, and distributed systems to deliver reliable engineering solutions. Your work will directly reduce operational friction and help development teams move faster and more securely. The environment is remote-first, collaborative, and highly technical, with a strong emphasis on ownership and continuous improvement. This position is open to candidates residing in Australia or New Zealand. Develop internal developer tooling: Build and maintain high-performance Go-based APIs, microservices, and CLI applications that automate processes, reduce friction, and improve engineering productivity. Build scalable automation: Design systems that orchestrate workflows across systems of record, SaaS platforms, internal infrastructure, and other engineering services. Implement governance-as-code: Develop automated solutions for repository and service governance, helping maintain consistent, secure, and scalable engineering standards. Enable self-service infrastructure: Create secure interfaces and abstractions that allow engineering teams to request and manage infrastructure resources independently. Design and maintain backend platforms: Develop reliable services and APIs using Go, with a focus on scalability, maintainability, performance, and resilience. Operate and optimize systems: Deploy and support backend services running on Kubernetes/EKS, taking ownership of performance profiling, debugging, tuning, and reliability. Collaborate across teams: Partner with engineering and other cross-functional teams to understand developer needs, identify bottlenecks, and deliver practical platform solutions. Champion Platform as a Product: Continuously identify opportunities to improve the developer lifecycle through automation, self-service capabilities, and thoughtful platform design. Requirements: Professional experience: Proven professional experience as a Backend Software Engineer using Go in production environments. Education: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience. Backend engineering: Strong experience building scalable web services, RESTful APIs, microservices, and distributed systems. Kubernetes: Demonstrated experience developing or operating services on Kubernetes. API expertise: Strong understanding of API design and consumption, including authentication and authorization mechanisms. Databases: Hands-on experience with database management, schema design, query optimization, and database performance tuning. Cloud & infrastructure: Experience managing infrastructure on AWS and working with Kubernetes/EKS. Developer platforms: Experience building internal developer tools, automation solutions, or CLI applications is highly relevant. DevOps practices: Solid knowledge of Git, version control, and continuous integration/continuous delivery. Performance engineering: Experience using profiling and debugging tools to identify bottlenecks and optimize system performance. Problem-solving: Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, with a focus on producing high-quality, maintainable solutions in a fast-paced environment. Communication: Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively across teams and time zones. Platform mindset: Genuine interest in Platform as a Product and enthusiasm for identifying developer pain points and solving them

jobgether-jobgether:lever:c3768abf-ec0d-.description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Proven track record of delivering complex initiatives at scale, including ownership of externally committed milestones such as general availability launches, major releases, or regulated enterprise deadlines. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with engineers, product managers, executives, and customer-facing stakeholders. jobgether-jobgether:lever:ede4e870-fcd7-.title: Product Security & Compliance Engineer
jobgether-jobgether:lever:ede4e870-fcd7-.description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Product Security & Compliance Engineer based in Germany. This role combines hands-on product security engineering with cybersecurity compliance across connected hardware and cloud services. You will help build secure, resilient products while ensuring they meet evolving regulatory and cybersecurity requirements. Your work will span embedded devices, firmware, networking, software dependencies, and cloud services. You’ll conduct threat modeling, security validation, vulnerability assessments, and supply-chain risk management while translating findings into practical controls. The role also involves preparing technical evidence and documentation for product conformity and regulatory assessments. You’ll collaborate closely with hardware, firmware, cloud, product, external manufacturing, and certification teams in a distributed environment. It is an opportunity to take meaningful ownership at the intersection of product security, compliance, connected technology, and privacy. Own cybersecurity aspects of regulatory compliance for connected hardware products, including RED cybersecurity requirements and EN 18031. Support preparation for the EU Cyber Resilience Act, covering vulnerability management, security updates, Software Bills of Materials, support periods, and incident reporting. Create and maintain architecture and data-flow diagrams for connected products and associated services. Conduct threat modeling and translate identified risks into actionable security requirements, controls, and engineering priorities. Perform hands-on product security validation, including vulnerability and dependency scanning, SAST/DAST, software composition analysis, firmware analysis, network and service exposure assessments, and targeted penetration testing. Generate, maintain, and monitor SBOMs to identify and manage vulnerabilities within software dependencies. Validate security mechanisms including authentication, secure boot, and signed software or firmware updates. Translate security assessments and testing results into compliance evidence, technical documentation, risk assessments, conformity assessments, and Declarations of Conformity. Partner with hardware, firmware, cloud, and product engineering teams to embed security and compliance requirements early in the development lifecycle. Coordinate with external manufacturing partners and certification bodies while maintaining internal ownership of cybersecurity evidence. Collaborate with open-source communities and related projects to ensure security information, vulnerability handling, and software documentation are effectively maintained. Track product conformity status, security support periods, regulatory deadlines, and changes that may require reassessment. Provide privacy-by-design guidance for significant changes to cloud and software services when required. Requirements Strong hands-on technical experience in at least one security domain, such as embedded/firmware security, network security, application security, or cloud security. Experience creating architecture or data-flow diagrams and conducting threat modeling for real-world products or systems. Practical experience with security testing and tools, including vulnerability scanning, SAST/DAST, software composition analysis, SBOM tooling, network security testing, firmware analysis, or penetration testing. southparkcommons-cognition-ai:ashbyhq:23.title: Brand Marketer
southparkcommons-cognition-ai:ashbyhq:23.description: WE ARE AN APPLIED AI LAB BUILDING END-TO-END SOFTWARE AGENTS. We're the makers of Devin, the first AI software engineer. Our team is extremely talent-dense. Among our founding team, we have world-class competitive programmers, former founders, and leaders from companies at the cutting edge of AI including Scale AI, Palantir, Cursor, Waymo, Tesla, Lunchclub, Modal, Google DeepMind, and Nuro. Building Devin is just the first step—our hardest challenges still lie ahead. If you’re excited to solve some of the world’s biggest problems and build AI that can reason on real-world tasks, apply to join us. ABOUT THE ROLE We're looking for a creative, strategic marketer to own how Cognition shows up to developers, from product launches and brand campaigns to the day-to-day work of figuring out what we say, how we say it, and where. You'll plan and execute integrated campaigns across channels and work closely with our creative agencies and growth team to turn big ideas into things people actually see and remember. You might: - Plan and execute product launches end-to-end, coordinating messaging, creative, channels, timing, and cross-functional teams to make launches land. We have two major ones in the next 90 days. - Define campaign strategy: what's the insight, what's the message, who's the audience, and how does it come to life across paid, organic, out-of-home, events, and partnerships. - Be the strategic counterpart to our creative agencies: set the brief, give sharp feedback, and make sure the work that comes back is on-strategy and on-brand. - Own upper funnel brand awareness programs, like out-of-home marketing. - Develop messaging and positioning for specific campaigns, translating product capabilities into copy that resonates with developers and engineering leaders. - Scope and produce video content for campaigns, working with our in-house team and external partners to create ads, product demos, and launch videos. - Build, execute, and improve the marketing campaign playbook: templates, timelines, checklists, and processes that let a tiny team punch way above its weight. You should be: - A creative strategist. You can look at a product and figure out what's interesting about it, who cares, and how to make them pay attention. You have taste. - An executor. Big ideas are worthless without follow-through. You can manage a campaign from brief to launch with dozens of moving pieces and not drop things. - AI-native. You use AI tools daily and are excited to work at a company where the product is AI. Your instinct is to automate everything. - A clear writer. Good campaigns start with good copy. You can write a headline, a brief, an email, or a landing page and make it sharp. - Comfortable with ambiguity. You'll help build our brand as we deploy it, adapting to the market’s response and what resonates with our customers. You might have: - 0-4 years of experience: we care more about taste, speed, and creative instinct than years on a resume - Run or meaningfully contributed to a product launch, brand campaign, or creative project - Written copy that has attracted attention, whether on X, a blog, or in marketing media like ads, landing pages, emails, briefs, anything - Worked with creative agencies or external partners - A portfolio, blog, side project, or body of work that shows how you think EQUAL OPPORTUNITY Cognition is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities throughout the hiring process - please let us know if you need any.

southparkcommons-cognition-ai:ashbyhq:4f.description: WE ARE AN APPLIED AI LAB BUILDING END-TO-END SOFTWARE AGENTS. We're the makers of Devin, the first AI software engineer. Our team is extremely talent-dense. Among our founding team, we have world-class competitive programmers, former founders, and leaders from companies at the cutting edge of AI including Scale AI, Palantir, Cursor, Waymo, Tesla, Lunchclub, Modal, Google DeepMind, and Nuro. Building Devin is just the first step—our hardest challenges still lie ahead. If you’re excited to solve some of the world’s biggest problems and build AI that can reason on real-world tasks, apply to join us. WE ARE AN APPLIED AI LAB BUILDING END-TO-END SOFTWARE AGENTS. Software is how the modern world runs—but there's not enough of it, and too much of what exists isn't good enough. Banks and governments still run COBOL from the 1970s. Budgets go to technical debt and maintenance instead of the features customers actually want. The bottleneck has always been the same: engineering talent is scarce and expensive, and budgets only stretch so far. AI agents make it possible to build more software, faster, at higher quality—and Cognition is at the center of that shift. We built Devin, the first AI software engineer, and we're working with some of the world's largest enterprises to fundamentally expand what their engineering organizations can deliver. Our strategy is centered on high-end, curated executive experiences with differentiated content, standout hospitality, and deliberate guest lists. You will help us create the spaces where the most influential engineering and technology leaders come together to understand what comes next. This role is execution-heavy. We are looking for someone who obsesses over details, runs flawless programs end to end, thrives under pressure, and coordinates cross-functional teams with precision.
